# USB access, installation, and recovery

## Setup and safety

Use Python and the official `mpremote` tool. If it is missing, install it in
an isolated environment rather than overriding the system Python's safeguards:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install mpremote
.venv/bin/mpremote devs
```

On Windows use `python -m venv .venv`, then
`.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install mpremote` and
`.venv\Scripts\mpremote devs`. Commands below use `mpremote` as shorthand for
the executable in that environment. Keep the environment out of source control.

Use the detected port, not a remembered one. The tested 2025 badge reports
USB `2e8a:0005`, product `GitHub Badger MicroPython`. Typical port paths are
`/dev/cu.usbmodem...`, `/dev/ttyACM...`, or `COM...`.

Only one process can own the serial port. Close other serial tools before
connecting. Do not run these commands in parallel or send raw binary to the
interactive prompt. Use remote paths beginning with `:` for `mpremote fs`.

## Read-only inspection

```bash
mpremote connect PORT resume exec "import sys; print(sys.version)"
mpremote connect PORT resume exec "import badgeware; print(dir(badgeware)); print(dir(badgeware.io))"
mpremote connect PORT resume exec "import badgeware; print(badgeware.os.listdir('/system/apps'))"
mpremote connect PORT resume exec "print(open('/system/main.py').read())"
mpremote connect PORT resume exec "print(open('/system/apps/menu/__init__.py').read())"
```

The tested 2025 badge needed `resume` after a normal command failed with
`could not enter raw repl`. It also raised
`TypeError: can't convert 'NoneType' object to str implicitly` during some
ordinary module imports in the interrupted runtime. Access through the
already loaded `badgeware.os` allowed directory inspection without changing
files. Do not describe that error as a missing filesystem or erase the badge
to fix it.

These are observed workarounds, not guarantees for every build. If access
still fails, check the port and ownership, then ask for a normal RESET and
retry. Stop repeated unsuccessful probes and report the exact error.
Do not inspect or display secrets or saved personal data.

Finish serial inspection with:

```bash
mpremote connect PORT reset
```

## Install one app through USB Disk Mode

1. Inspect the installed menu first. The tested stock menu has six hard-coded
   entries and already loads PNG icons. A new directory alone will not appear.
   Explain this before copying. If a menu change is needed, agree on it with
   the user and back up the installed file first. Do not silently replace it
   with the repo's paginated version or remove an existing app entry.
2. Quickly press RESET twice. The 2025 docs say this opens USB Disk Mode,
   exposing the `BADGER` volume. The tested 2025 `powman` does **not** export
   `reset_into_msc`; do not use the 2026 remote disk-mode command.
3. Confirm the mounted badge volume contains `apps/`. Do not guess its mount
   path or drive letter. If the layout differs, inspect and stop before
   writing to an uncertain target.
4. Confirm the destination is `BADGER`, **not** the `RP2350` bootloader drive.
   Copy only the requested app into `apps/<name>/`. Preview the source and
   destination first. Back up an existing destination before replacement;
   never delete it first. Exclude secrets, dotfiles, caches, virtual
   environments, and host-generated bytecode.
5. Check the installed `__init__.py`, assets, and 24x24 PNG icon against the
   source. Do not copy the whole repository or the whole `badge25/` tree.
6. Flush and eject using the host's supported eject action. On macOS,
   `diskutil eject /Volumes/BADGER` applies only after confirming that mount.
   On Windows, use the drive's Eject action; on Linux, use the file manager
   or the verified volume's unmount/eject command.
7. Wait for the volume to disappear. Press RESET if needed. Rediscover the
   serial port, verify installed files when accessible, then issue
   `mpremote connect PORT reset` to leave the badge running normally.
8. Open the menu and verify the tile, correct icon, launch, controls, HOME,
   reopen, and saved data. Request the user's visual confirmation when needed.

Do not apply `hyb26-skill`'s icon patch: the 2025 menu is a different program.

## Firmware recovery is a separate task

Do not flash firmware during app development unless the user explicitly asks.
Firmware containing a filesystem may replace apps and saved files.

The 2025 repo docs describe holding HOME, pressing and releasing RESET, then
releasing HOME to expose `RP2350`. HOME acts as BOOTSEL in that procedure.
If a button is missing, do not instruct the user to bridge contacts or assume
there is another accessible BOOTSEL button.

If serial works, first check whether `machine.bootloader` exists. Calling it
is a firmware-mode change and needs a recovery request, not just inspection.
It worked on a previously tested 2026 badge; it has **not** been verified on
the connected 2025 badge. Do not promise it works there.

Before any firmware copy, confirm the exact UF2 file and evidence that it is
for the **2025** hardware. Use a year-specific release, not "latest" without
checking the target. A name such as `badger-...-with-filesystem.uf2` is not proof
of the year. Never substitute 2026 firmware or a flash-erasing UF2. Back up
user files where possible and explain any remaining data-loss risk.

Copy firmware only to a verified bootloader volume. Wait for restart, then
check the firmware identity and normal startup. A USB disconnect during
reboot can be expected, but does not by itself prove a successful flash.
